sentences.ko: 그러니까 부탁할게, 나 판단하기 전에 잠깐만 생각해 줘.
sentences.text: So, I'm asking you, please just take a moment before you judge me.

alts.text: Just hang on a sec before you judge me, okay?
I would ask that you please take a moment before you judge me.

sentences.note: **take a moment**는 '잠깐 시간을 두고 생각하다'라는 뜻으로, 오해받을 만한 얘기를 꺼내기 직전에 씁니다. **before you judge me**를 붙이면 '내 말 끝까지 들어 줘'라는 부탁이 됩니다.
sentences.situation: The Ones with the Whole Gang from Season 5 | Friends

sentences.ko: 진짜라니까, 저 여자가 나한테 완전 윙크했어.
sentences.text: I'm telling you, that girl totally winked at me.

alts.text: Seriously, she totally winked at me.
I assure you, that young woman winked at me.

sentences.note: **I'm telling you**는 상대가 내 말을 안 믿을 때 '진짜라니까' 하고 밀어붙이는 말입니다. **totally**는 우리말 '완전'처럼 말에 힘을 줄 때 씁니다.
sentences.situation: The Ones with the Whole Gang from Season 3 | Friends

sentences.ko: 나 어렸을 때부터 발가락으로 동전 집을 수 있었어.
sentences.text: ever since I was little, I've been able to pick up quarters with my toes.

alts.text: I've always been able to grab quarters with my toes, since I was a kid.
Since I was a small child, I have been able to pick up quarters with my toes.

sentences.note: **ever since I was little**는 '어렸을 때부터 쭉'이라는 뜻으로, 자기 특기나 오래된 버릇을 말할 때 씁니다. **pick up**은 바닥에 있는 것을 '집어 올리다'입니다.
sentences.situation: The Ones That Make You Laugh: Part 3 | Friends

sentences.ko: 나 내일 밤에 데이트가 있는데, 좀 멋있어 보여야 하거든.
sentences.text: I have this date tomorrow night and and I have to look cool.

alts.text: Got a date tomorrow night, so I gotta look cool.
Tomorrow evening I have a date, and I need to look cool.

sentences.note: **I have this date**처럼 a 대신 this를 쓰면 상대가 모르는 일을 처음 꺼낼 때 '있잖아, 데이트가 하나 있는데' 하는 느낌이 납니다. **look cool**은 옷차림이나 분위기가 '멋있어 보이다'라는 말입니다.
sentences.situation: The Ones with the Whole Gang from Season 10 | Friends

sentences.ko: 둘 다 제발 좀 어른답게 굴 수 없어?
sentences.text: Would you both please start acting like adults?

alts.text: Come on, you two, grow up already.
I would ask that both of you begin behaving like adults.

sentences.note: **acting like adults**는 유치하게 싸우는 두 사람에게 '어른답게 좀 굴어'라고 할 때 씁니다. 더 짧게는 **grow up**이라고 합니다.
sentences.situation: The Ones That Make You Laugh: Part 3 | Friends

sentences.text: Why don't you just let me take care of the presentation?

alts.text: Just leave the presentation to me.
Perhaps you could allow me to handle the presentation.

sentences.note: **Why don't you just let me**는 '그냥 나한테 맡겨'라고 부드럽게 나설 때 쓰는 말입니다. **take care of**는 일을 맡아서 처리한다는 뜻으로 회사에서도 집에서도 흔히 씁니다.
sentences.situation: The Ones That Make You Laugh: Part 3 | Friends

sentences.ko: 아니 그러니까, 너 그 여자랑 결혼할 것 같아?
sentences.text: I mean, like, do you see yourself marrying her?

alts.text: So, could you picture marrying her?
Can you imagine yourself marrying her someday?

sentences.note: **see yourself marrying**은 '네가 ~하는 모습이 그려지냐', 즉 앞으로 그럴 것 같냐고 물을 때 씁니다. 진로나 미래 얘기에서 Do you see yourself ~? 꼴로 자주 나옵니다.
sentences.situation: The Ones That Make You Laugh: Part 3 | Friends

sentences.ko: 너네는 왜 한 번도 우리랑 포커를 안 쳤어?
sentences.text: HOW COME YOU GUYS HAVE NEVER PLAYED poker with us?

alts.text: Wait, you guys never played poker with us?
Why is it that you have never played poker with us?

sentences.note: **HOW COME**은 why와 뜻이 같지만 더 편하게, 좀 의아하다는 느낌으로 묻는 말입니다. 뒤에 질문 어순이 아니라 평서문 어순이 온다는 점이 why와 다릅니다.
sentences.situation: The Ones with the Whole Gang from Season 1 | Friends

sentences.ko: 우리가 음… 스키 타러 가자고 초대를 좀 받긴 했거든.
sentences.text: We were um sort of invited to go skiing.

alts.text: Someone kinda asked us to go skiing.
In a way, we received an invitation to go skiing.

sentences.note: **sort of**를 넣으면 '좀, 어떻게 보면' 하고 말을 흐리게 됩니다. 이미 약속이 있다고 미안해하며 말을 꺼낼 때 이렇게 돌려 말합니다.
sentences.situation: The Ones with the Whole Gang from Season 3 | Friends
